name: Powdery Mildew of Garden Egg
description: A common fungal disease that appears as a white powdery coating on garden egg leaves. The disease thrives in warm, dry weather and can significantly reduce yields by stressing the plant and reducing fruit size.
symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces
Powdery coating spreading to cover entire leaves
Leaves turning yellow and drying from edges
Stunted growth of new leaves and shoots
Premature leaf drop in severe cases
causes: Warm dry days with cool humid nights
Dense planting with poor air circulation
treatments: Spray neem oil solution (5ml/L water) weekly
Apply potassium bicarbonate solution (1 tsp/L water)
prevention: Maintain proper plant spacing for air flow
Remove and destroy infected leaves promptly
